toc.title: How Terraform uses providers at run time

html:
1What a provider is

A provider is a plugin that lets Terraform talk to an API (a cloud, a SaaS service, a platform). Terraform core reads the configuration and builds the plan; providers create, read, update and delete the real resources.

Fact Detail
Where providers come from The Terraform Registry (registry.terraform.io) by default
Tiers Official (HashiCorp), partner (a technology company), community
Source address namespace/type, for example hashicorp/aws
Downloaded by terraform init
What a provider defines Resource types and data sources, such as aws_instance
Exam tip

. Terraform core does not know any cloud; providers do. terraform init downloads the providers.

2Installing and versioning providers

You declare the providers a configuration needs in a terraform block with required_providers, and configure them in provider blocks.

terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.12"
  required_providers {
    aws = {
      source  = "hashicorp/aws"
      version = "~> 5.0"
    }
  }
}

provider "aws" {
  region = "us-east-1"
}
Part Meaning
required_version The Terraform CLI versions allowed
required_providers Which providers, where from (source) and which versions (version)
provider block Configuration of one provider: region, credentials, endpoints

Version constraints:

Operator Meaning
= or no operator Exactly that version
!= Anything except that version
>, >=, <, <= Comparisons
~> Pessimistic constraint: allow only the rightmost version part to increase; ~> 5.0 means at least 5.0 and below 6.0; ~> 5.1.0 means at least 5.1.0 and below 5.2
Exam tip

. ~> 5.0 allows 5.1, 5.2 and so on, but not 6.0. Pin versions so that a new provider release does not change your infrastructure unexpectedly.

3The dependency lock file

terraform init writes .terraform.lock.hcl, which records the exact provider versions and checksums that were selected.

Fact Detail
Purpose Same provider versions for every run and every team member
Commit it? Yes, commit it to version control
Update it terraform init -upgrade selects newer versions that match the constraints
Do not edit by hand Terraform maintains it

4Using several providers

Case How
Different providers List each in required_providers and configure each (for example aws and random)
Same provider, several configurations Add alias to extra provider blocks (for example two regions) and choose with the provider meta-argument 
provider "aws" {
  region = "us-east-1"
}

provider "aws" {
  alias  = "west"
  region = "us-west-2"
}

resource "aws_s3_bucket" "backup" {
  provider = aws.west
  bucket   = "example-backup-bucket"
}

A resource without a provider argument uses the default (unaliased) configuration of its provider.

Exam tip

. Aliases are for several configurations of the same provider, such as two regions. Use provider = aws.west on the resource.

5How Terraform uses providers at run time

Step What happens
init Terraform installs providers and records versions in the lock file
plan The provider reads current infrastructure and Terraform compares it with the configuration
apply The provider makes the API calls to create, update or destroy

terraform providers lists the providers a configuration uses.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Which command downloads the providers that a configuration needs?

  • Aterraform plan
  • Bterraform fmt
  • Cterraform init
  • Dterraform output
Show the answer

Answer: C. terraform init installs the required providers and modules and creates the lock file.

S2A configuration states version = "~> 5.0" for a provider. Which versions are allowed?

  • AAny version from 5.0 up to but not including 6.0
  • BOnly version 5.0 exactly
  • CAny version at or above 5.0, including version 6.0 and later
  • DOnly versions below 5.0
Show the answer

Answer: A. The pessimistic operator allows increases of the rightmost part only, so 5.0 up to below 6.0.

S3What does the dependency lock file record?

  • AThe selected provider versions and their checksums
  • BThe state of the deployed resources
  • CThe values of all input variables
  • DThe output values of the last apply
Show the answer

Answer: A. The lock file records which provider versions and checksums were selected, so everyone uses the same ones.

S4A team needs to create resources in two regions with the same provider. What should they use?

  • ATwo provider blocks, one with an alias
  • BTwo separate Terraform installations
  • CA different state file for every resource
  • DA data source for every region
Show the answer

Answer: A. An extra provider block with an alias gives a second configuration, selected by the provider argument.

S5Which command updates the selected provider versions within the allowed constraints?

  • Aterraform init -upgrade
  • Bterraform fmt -upgrade
  • Cterraform plan -upgrade
  • Dterraform validate -upgrade
Show the answer

Answer: A. terraform init -upgrade chooses the newest versions that match the constraints and updates the lock file.

S6Where does Terraform download providers from by default?

  • AThe local state file
  • BThe cloud console of each provider
  • CThe Terraform Registry
  • DThe version control system of the team
Show the answer

Answer: C. Providers are downloaded from the Terraform Registry unless another source is configured.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What does a provider do?

Show the answer

Lets Terraform talk to an API and manage its resources.

R2What block lists the required providers?

Show the answer

required_providers inside the terraform block.

R3What file records provider versions?

Show the answer

.terraform.lock.hcl.

R4What does ~> 5.0 mean?

Show the answer

At least 5.0 and below 6.0.

R5What is a provider alias for?

Show the answer

Several configurations of the same provider.

R6Should the lock file be committed?

Show the answer

Yes.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Providers plugins from the Registry; installed by init; define resource types
Declare required_providers with source and version; provider block configures
Constraints =, !=, comparisons, ~> (rightmost part only)
Lock file .terraform.lock.hcl; commit; init -upgrade to move forward
Several different providers listed; same provider with alias and provider =
